title: Half-life of a Radioactive Sample
learningObjectives: Explain that half-life is the time required for half of a radioactive substance to decay
Apply the exponential decay relation N=N0*(1/2)^(t/T) to determine remaining amount
Compare short and long half-life isotopes and how remaining amount depends on elapsed time

explanations.text: For the studied material, the half-life describes how quickly the amount decreases: after one half-life half remains, after two half-lives one quarter remains, following the rule that half the radioactivity decays in one half-life interval.

evidence.quote: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years (half the radioactivity will decay in 30 years).

explanations.text: Different isotopes illustrate the range of decay rates: some have half-lives of decades while others persist for thousands of years, so the remaining hazard depends on both the initial amount and the isotope-specific half-life.

evidence.quote: Plutonium-239 has a half-life of 24,000 years.
Transuranic wastes, sometimes called TRU, account for most of the radioactive hazard remaining in high-level waste after 1,000 years.

explanations.text: The underlying process is that unstable atoms disintegrate over time toward stable forms, which is why the amount remaining can be modeled by exponential decay.

evidence.quote: Radioactive isotopes eventually decay, or disintegrate, to harmless materials.

predictions.prompt: Predict remaining after half a half-life
